fact: 2010-04-17（周六）：Clare 38、Beck 34、Alba 8 岁；本章视角换成 **Beck 第一人称**（章首署“Beck:”），Clare 邀她来自己工作室。
quote: Saturday, April 17, 2010 (Clare is 38, Beck is 34, Alba is 8) ... Beck: Clare has invited me to visit her studio.

fact: Clare 家是红砖平房，绿色西班牙式屋顶瓦、黄色饰边；工作室在她家后院，由车库改建；Beck 按指示走侧道到屋后敲门，Clare 开门说“Come in… Watch the steps.”
quote: Her house is a pretty, redbrick bungalow with those fancy green Spanish roof tiles and yellow trim. I walk along a side path to the back of the house per her instructions and find a garage-like building that’s been converted into a studio.

fact: 进屋先见红漆小桌、黑陶瓶与未点的蜡烛；Beck 把包和墨镜放在瓶边，Clare 皱眉但没说话，Beck 就把东西挪到地上。
quote: The first thing I see is a small red lacquered table that holds a black ceramic vase and an unlit candle. I set my purse and my sunglasses next to the vase. I see Clare frown but she doesn’t say anything. I pick up my stuff and put it on the floor.
anchor: It’s a bright warm morning, and as I step into the little building

fact: Clare 先关掉一些灯，问 Beck 有没有恐惧症，让她闭眼，牵着她（Clare 手凉而干、Beck 手热而汗）绕行木地板到房间中央，再让她睁眼。
quote: Clare says, “Hang on, I should turn off some lights before you take another step. Okay. Wait. You don’t have any phobias, do you? No? Good. Close your eyes.” ... Clare takes my hot sweaty hand into her cool dry one and leads me across a wood floor in a winding path.
anchor: I warily squinch my eyes closed

fact: 睁眼所见：成百上千只黑色小鸟（比乌鸦小）悬在细钢丝上、翅膀固定地作飞行动作；Clare 按遥控器，顶灯亮成暮色，天花板附近有马达声，整群鸟绕着两人极缓慢旋转、聚散起伏，伴着鸟叫声；Beck 觉得自己站在悬崖边要掉下去，Clare 伸手抓住她，再按遥控让一切停下。
quote: There are hundreds, maybe thousands of them. As my eyes adjust, I see that they are birds in flight: each one is rotating, vibrating with slight air currents, hanging from thin wires; puppets. ... The whole flock of birds begins to move around us, very slowly.
anchor: We are surrounded by black shapes; the shapes are suspended in the air

fact: Clare 领她到有巨大窗户、佩斯利花纹沙发和绘图桌的小办公室，到处是布料、纸、毛毡、干花、颜料罐，“像化学实验室或女巫的厨房”；两人喝冰白葡萄酒，安静了几分钟。
quote: She leads me out of the room into a small office area with huge windows and a paisley covered sofa and a drawing table ... that remind me of a chemistry lab or a witch’s kitchen. ... Clare sits next to me, and we clink glasses and drink in silence for a few minutes.

fact: Beck 自陈是贵格会信徒（Quaker），一向觉得安静最能恢复精神；她回忆当初在 Ando Gallery 与 Clare 同坐不说话时就很愉快，此刻在这间小办公室里觉得兴奋，Clare 等着她把话想清楚。
quote: As a Quaker, I have always found quiet very restorative; I crave it. ... When I first sat with Clare in the Ando Gallery I remember thinking how pleasant it was to abide there with her without speaking.
anchor: Most people find it difficult to be in a room and not rush

fact: 作品名叫 murmuration（鸟群齐飞）；Clare 用一根食指在手机上点，给 Beck 看真实椋鸟群的视频：黑点从树梢升起，聚成椭圆、锥形、蘑菇形，“像一只纯几何的生物，在半空中不断改变主意”。Clare 解释可能是有猛禽，并说有“flocking behavior”这门学科。
quote: “It’s a murmuration,” Clare tells me. ... a swarm of black specks rise up from the trees, forming a diffuse, dark cloud that coalesces into an oval, then a cone, a mushroom . . . ... “Probably there is a predator, maybe a hawk. There’s a whole scientific discipline, flocking behavior, that tries to explain it,”
anchor: I notice that she types with one index finger

fact: 转折点（动机段）：Clare 说这装置就是她长期的感觉——“很久都安顿不下来，像被什么看不见的东西追逼”，她想站在那东西的中心、站在鸟暴的风眼里；并说自己不是要让人平静，而是“想把我的 blackness 外化，放到别人看得见的地方”。
quote: “That’s how I’ve been feeling for a long while now,” Clare says. “For the longest time I couldn’t settle—I felt as though I was being harried by something I couldn’t see. I wanted to stand in the center of the thing, to be in the eye of a storm of birds.” ... “I wanted to take my blackness and externalize it—I wanted to put it where other people could see it.”

fact: Beck 以玩笑回应：“作为一个 Blackness 一直被人围观的人，你确定要这么做？”Clare 涨红脸盯着膝盖；Beck 道歉后看见她脸上“担忧、脆弱、赤裸的渴望”，伸手握住她的手，两人对视、把头各自歪向相反方向，放下酒杯靠近，接吻；Beck 觉得“在长久孤独之后找到了心灵的伴侣”。
quote: “Hmm. Speaking as someone whose Blackness is on display all the time, are you sure you want to do that?” ... And then we kiss and I feel I have found my heart’s companion after a long empty time alone.
anchor: I mean it as a joke but Clare turns bright red

fact: 两人整理衣服、尴尬地互相打趣（“I don’t usually—”“I’ve never—”“Not that I’m not cool with it—”），Clare 说“Let’s do that again”，于是又来一次；Beck 又待了一小时，直到 Clare 惊觉要去祖父家接上完课的 Alba，去晚了祖父会发脾气。
quote: Clare says, “I don’t usually—” just as I say, “I’ve never—” ... and Clare says, “Let’s do that again,” and we do. ... “Ohmygod, the time! I have to pick up Alba, she’s at her grandfather’s having a lesson and he gets crabby if I’m late.”
anchor: We sit up, smile shyly at each other’s surprise

fact: 送别：两人一起走到车边，Beck 犹豫能不能当众吻她，Clare 说“I guess we’ll have to figure some things out.”；Beck 只在她耳边落下一吻，口红蹭到她脸颊上，用手指擦掉——反而成了最亲密的一下；Clare 喊“I’ll phone you tonight!”，Beck 大声答“Yes!”，从后视镜里看她开车走，想着在她打电话前的空白几小时里该做什么，“and this is how we begin.”
quote: She says, “I guess we’ll have to figure some things out.” She embraces me and I manage to land a kiss near her ear, leaving a dark red lipstick smear on her cheek. ... Clare calls after me, “I’ll phone you tonight!”
anchor: As I lean in to kiss her goodbye I wonder can I kiss her in public
